the governance of FTSEs in Belgium and the relationship between their governance, resources and goals.
the governance of FTSEs in Belgium, and the way in which this relates to the resources and goals of the organisations.
the governance of FTSEs and the link between governance and organisational characteristics.

the governance of FTSEs is not a one‐size‐fits‐all model.

the three governance models are not only different, but also that they are not equally efficient in achieving the social and environmental goals of the organisations.Originality/value – The paper is one of the first to investigate the governance of social enterprises in the fair trade sector, and to link governance to other organisational features and to the social and environmental objectives.
the governance of FTSEs is not yet sufficiently developed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an understanding of what the governance of FTSEs is, and how it differs from that of traditional social enterprises.
we have been able to show that the governance structure of FTSEs can be described as a multi-stakeholder structure in which the different stakeholder groups are involved to a different degree.
the governance of FTSEs is not only a matter of the composition of the board of directors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the governance of FTSEs is not only a question of formal structures, but also a question of how the governance structure interacts with the organisation's goals and resources, and how it is linked to its activities.
the governance structures of the FTSEs we studied reflect a mix of the three governance paradigms we identified: managerial, volunteer‐based and multi‐stakeholders.
the current literature on social enterprise governance does not adequately reflect the governance reality of the social enterprise sector.
